For 0<=rho<=2, the elementary hyperbolic inequality makes F_rho strictly increasing from B+C*rho to infinity and proves the exhaustive one-/two-mode alternative, including quartic-flat equality. For each real rho>2, the explicit admissible b-family gives derivative signs negative near origin, positive at some finite point, then negative at infinity, proving at least three strict modes. Normalizability follows from positive outward rate-drift asymptotics. An exact rational witness and 688 diagnostic assertions corroborate but do not replace the continuum proof.

originality.rationale: The original arXiv:2405.13521v2 full HTML Sections II-III and Appendix A give the stationary distribution, the center-curvature test and an explicitly conditional one/two-mode inference; they do not prove the sharp gradient-ratio threshold. The closest 2026-11-08 published mathematical RESULT.md proves a g=3u trimodal window and a no-trimodality statement only for 0<=g<=u. Its proof and assumptions were read: neither implication contains all 0<=g<=2u, nor the existence of >=3 peaks for each real g/u>2. The new theorem is the maximal guaranteed gradient ratio, with its sharp physical existence converse. Other indexed related processes do not imply these two universal statements. Unindexed equivalent literature remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: Relevant unindexed or inaccessible publications could independently establish the sharp gradient ratio two.

The matched 2026-11-08 published result establishes a restricted g=3u example, so novelty must remain the universal separation and full g<=2u classification; the explicit rational witness alone is covered.
The upper-mode count for arbitrary g>2u is not claimed.

value.rationale: The original stochastic active-matter paper left the global mode count conditional; a later mathematical phase diagram resolved a specific g=3u case but excluded trimodality only for g<=u. The new proof identifies an exact maximal robust ratio two, doubles the rigorously classified gradient domain, and proves sharp physical accessibility of additional phases at every larger ratio, rather than a numerical slice or renamed known threshold. The distinction is useful for deciding when local curvature completely determines observable stationary modality.
